title: Derivative Moments and Influence
statement: Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ take values in $\{-1,1\}$, let $i\in[n]$, and let $p\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $p>0$. Then $\mathbb E|D_i f|^p=\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]$, with uniform expectation on the cube, where $D_i f(x)=(f(x^{i\mapsto 0})-f(x^{i\mapsto 1}))/2$ and $\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]=\mathbb E[(f(x)-f(x^i))^2/4]$, with $x^i$ obtained by flipping coordinate $i$.
hypotheses_covered: f takes only the values −1 and 1
replaced: Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube, $i\in[n]$, and $p>0$. Then $\mathbb E|D_if|^p=I_i(f)$, where $D_if(x)=(f(x^{i\leftarrow0})-f(x^{i\leftarrow1}))/2$. For a real cube function $h$, define $I_i(h)=\tfrac14\mathbb E_x(h(x)-h(x^{(i)}))^2$, where $x^{(i)}$ flips coordinate $i$ and $\mathbb E_x$ is uniform expectation.
